summary.headline: Windlas Biotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% y-o-y to INR264 crore, with CDMO up 34% to INR215 crore and H1 crossing INR500 crore for the first time.
summary.overview: Management reported its 15th consecutive quarter of record revenue, with Q2 FY27 revenue up 19% y-o-y to INR264 crore and H1 FY27 up 18% to INR512 crore. Growth was led by the generic formulation CDMO vertical (Q2 up 34% to INR215 crore), while trade generics fell to INR36 crore in Q2 as codeine-based products were phased out. Adjusted EBITDA (excluding non-cash ESOP cost) was 13.7% in both Q2 and H1, and reported EBITDA was INR29 crore in Q2. Plant 6 was commercialised in late September 2026, and Plant 4 and Plant 5 (injectables) received EU GMP certification.

segments.name: Generic formulation CDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR215 crore (+34% y-o-y); H1 INR422 crore (+32%). Management attributed growth to a larger share of customer portfolios and new products, with no single one-off driver.

segments.name: Trade generics and institutional
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR36 crore and H1 INR66 crore, held back by the exit from codeine-based products that are being replaced with new non-codeine launches. Management previously aspired to about INR200 crore annual revenue in FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR12 crore (+26%); H1 INR23 crore (+46%). Smallest vertical; growth depends on dossier approvals, product registrations and site approvals, which are described as binary.

segments.name: Injectables (Plant 4 and Plant 5)
segments.commentary: Both plants received EU GMP certification in Q2 FY27; injectables have so far served mainly the domestic market. EU product-level approvals are still pending, with filings made.

segments.name: Plant 6 (oral solids)
segments.commentary: Commercialised on about 28 September 2026, so operating costs and depreciation will flow into Q3 FY27. Capacity is 200 million tablets and capsules, with up to INR1,100 crore revenue potential at company level and up to 10% debottlenecking.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management declined to comment on CDMO momentum for H2 FY27 or FY28, and on when trade generics will return to the FY26 run-rate of about INR200 crore.
Management said trade generics growth in FY28 is an aspiration, but it does not want to give guidance on it.
Management said it expects to keep investing phase-wise, starting new oral solids capacity only once Plant 6 is fully utilised.
A new efficiency project involving capex of INR25-30 crore is expected to reduce opex, with more detail promised in coming quarters.
Expected Plant 6 opex to be absorbed as revenue ramps, which management said will drive EBITDA conversion.
Capital allocation priorities listed: acquisitions, capex for core dosage forms, internal new dosage form capex, buybacks when shares look undervalued, dividends and employee rewards.
capex_capacity: Plant 6 commercialised around 28 September 2026; capacity 200 million tablets and capsules, with up to INR1,100 crore revenue potential at company level and up to 10% capacity improvement possible.
Plant 4 and Plant 5 (injectables) received EU GMP certification in Q2 FY27, with the Philippines approval received earlier.
Plant 2 extension and the injectable facility expansion are progressing steadily.
No new oral solids capex has started; injectable expansion will follow once existing injectable capacity is maxed out.
Management is exploring acquisitions for other dosage forms, with nothing at a final stage; if none is found, it would build a new dosage form internally. Nothing has been initiated.
Maintenance capex is the expected baseline; a separate INR25-30 crore opex-reduction capex project is in progress.
demand_pricing: Indian pharma market volume growth was 2.3% in the quarter per management; an analyst cited 2.5%. Management said volume growth was flat to negative for about two to two and a half years.
API prices are volatile and vary across the company's 700-800 APIs; management declined to quantify the API price contribution to growth.
Management said it gained a higher share of CDMO business in Q1 and Q2, but it does not expect that share to be permanent.
Quality regulation tightened: the regulator is testing over 1 lakh samples a year versus about 20,000-30,000 previously, and management said Windlas is audited 70-80 times a year.
Management said trade generics recovery depends on wider SKU range, non-codeine cough syrups and syrups, and state-level geographic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Will Plant 6 capacity be expanded, and is exports a 10-15% revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant 6 can serve up to INR1,100 crore at company level, with up to 10% improvement possible. Capacity is added phase-wise as peak levels are reached. Management gave no export guidance, citing binary approval timelines.

qa_highlights.question: How much of CDMO growth came from market share gains versus API price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify this, saying there is no published outsourcing data. It said the share gain is not permanent and that API prices are highly distributed and volatile, so no price contribution was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: When can trade generics return to the about INR200 crore FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline. It said the codeine loss is industry-wide, and it is replacing revenue with broader SKUs and non-codeine syrups.

qa_highlights.question: Is the opex saving plan a capex project?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Komal Gupta confirmed it is an INR25-30 crore capex investment that should reduce operating expenditure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue innovator or early-stage development work and EU CDMO contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is doing clinical and bioequivalence work for customers and owns its process IP and regulatory approvals. It has no plans for innovator or early-stage development services in the next 4-5 years, and EU CDMO work is being pursued without any announcement.

qa_highlights.question: What are the injectable EU timelines and the domestic utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No EU product approvals have been received yet. Management declined to give timelines or the domestic utilisation and ramp-up, saying it would not guide. The EU model will be a mix of CDMO and partnerships using its own MAs.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company allocate capital given its cash and buyback history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said another buyback is possible but no decision has been made, and the dividend follows policy. Priorities are acquisitions, capacity capex, internal new dosage form capex, opportunistic buybacks and employee rewards.

risks_watch: Trade generics recovery is uncertain: revenue fell to INR36 crore in Q2 and the codeine exit continues, with no timeline given.
CDMO share gains may not be sustained; management said they are not permanent, and H2 momentum was not guided.
Plant 6 opex and depreciation will hit Q3 FY27 margins before revenue ramps.
EU injectable approvals are pending product by product, with no timeline shared; exports contribute about 5% of revenue.
Enforcement under Schedule M is tightening, which could benefit organised players but may bring plant shutdowns or hiccups.
Management was evasive on capacity ramp-up for injectables and on whether the ESOP cost will continue to affect reported margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and quality, but guarded on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to guide on CDMO momentum, trade generics recovery, EU timelines and API price effects, citing the risk of misleading the market.
key_quotes: Consistency is not the most exciting word in business, but it is the one our customers and shareholders value the most.
We would ensure that never happens.
We remain as focused on quality of our earnings as on the pace of our growth.
We have been more broad-based and more distributed in our approach.

adds.what: Plant 6 oral solids (tablets and capsules), 200 million units/yr capacity, up to INR1,100 crore company-level revenue potential

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management declined to comment on H2 FY27 CDMO momentum or trade generics recovery, while Plant 6 (200 million units, commercialised ~28 Sep 2026, flowing into Q3) and a INR25-30 crore opex-reduction project support growth, with Q2 revenue up 19% led by CDMO +34%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Plant 6 opex and depreciation hit Q3 FY27 before revenue ramps, and adjusted EBITDA held at 13.7% in Q2 and H1, but management says absorption as revenue ramps will drive conversion and an INR25-30 crore opex-reduction capex is in progress.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plant 6 (200 million tablets and capsules) was commercialised around 28 Sep 2026, with operating costs and depreciation flowing into Q3 FY27; Plant 4 and Plant 5 injectables are EU GMP certified and Plant 2 extension and injectable expansion are progressing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 19% to INR264 crore with CDMO up 34% to INR215 crore and H1 up 18% to INR512 crore, but management gave no CDMO H2 guidance and said share gains are not permanent.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said new oral solids capex starts only once Plant 6 is fully utilised, injectable expansion follows once current capacity is maxed, and acquisitions are being explored with nothing final; a separate INR25-30 crore opex-reduction capex is already in progress and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given and management declined to comment on H2 FY27 CDMO momentum or FY28 trends, so there is no basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade generics fell to INR36 crore in Q2 with the codeine exit ongoing and no recovery timeline, and Plant 6 costs hit Q3 before revenue ramps.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Trade generics are being replaced by non-codeine launches and broader SKUs and syrups, and CDMO growth came partly from new products, though no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: EU injectable approvals (Plant 4 and 5)
rows.why: Both injectable plants received EU GMP certification in Q2 FY27 and filings are made, but no product approvals have been received and no timeline was given.

rows.label: Exports growth
rows.why: Exports rose 26% to INR12 crore in Q2 and 46% to INR23 crore in H1, but growth depends on binary dossier and site approvals and exports are about 5% of revenue.

rows.label: Buyback decision
rows.why: Net liquidity was INR223 crore at half-year end and management said another buyback is possible but no decision has been made.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, EU GMP certifications and quality, but declined to guide on CDMO momentum, trade generics recovery, EU timelines and API price effects; analysts pushed on how much growth was share gain versus API pricing and on the trade generics timeline.
